headline: Bengaluru's developer ecosystem is perfectly positioned for AI agents—your first agentic product could ride a wave of 96/100 project potential straight into a funded startup.
why_now: GitHub activity and growth scores above 94 signal an accelerating technical frontier, while news mentions at 88 confirm mainstream attention is peaking. study: Master LangChain or AutoGen by building a simple single-agent that completes a real task (file processing, API calls) end-to-end
Study multi-agent orchestration patterns—how agents delegate, share context, and resolve conflicts—usingcrewAI or Microsoft Semantic Kernel
Learn tool-use fundamentals: function calling, API integration, and retrieval-augmented generation with real data sources
Explore agentic evaluation frameworks—how to benchmark reliability, cost, and task completion rates across agent configurations

build.title: TaskMind—An Autonomous Multi-Agent Project Manager
build.description: Agents that break down a product spec into tasks, assign them to specialized sub-agents, call real APIs (GitHub, Slack, Linear), and report completion with audit trails. Demonstrates true end-to-end task completion without human intervention—exactly what investors want to see for agentic infrastructure.
deliverables: live demo URL showing agents negotiating and completing a sample sprint
technical write-up on agent orchestration decisions and failure modes

publish: Open-source the core framework and post a detailed README to Hacker News and X with a 90-second demo video
Speak at your local Bengaluru AI meetup or present at a conference like AI Engineer Summit—the community activity score of 84 shows strong appetite
Submit the write-up to Towards Data Science or TheSequence newsletter, targeting the 88 news-mentions audience
Angel outreach: target 5-7 Bengaluru founders who recently raised for AI infrastructure—frame TaskMind as infrastructure, not a toy
confidence: High confidence, based on GitHub, Hugging Face, News/RSS.
